A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching core equations and experiments despite renaming. The supplied pages are readable, but v2 refers to appendices absent from its PDF, whereas v4 includes Appendices A–M. Earlier supplementary proofs and settings therefore cannot be compared directly.

before.justification: v2 reports original SHNN classification results, hyperlink-prediction experiments and ablations in Table 4, Figures 3–4 and Table 5, even though some baseline classification scores are borrowed.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and reports additional Trivago results, training-free module comparisons and supplementary benchmark results in Tables 4–6 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains parameter removal and linearisation followed by precomputed propagation using the same hyperedge-size weighting, symmetric normalisation, self-loops and residual mixture. v2's SHNN becomes the TF-MP-Module within TF-HNN; the task-specific training pipeline is unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds Trivago, an accommodation/browsing-session hypergraph with 172,738 nodes, for classification and hyperlink prediction. Appendix J also extends hyperlink prediction from Cora-CA, Citeseer and House to DBLP-CA, Congress and Senate. The original classification datasets remain.

E2.justification: v4 evaluates SGC and SIGN with clique expansion in Table 6 and adds HyperGCL and HDSode classification comparisons in Appendix J. The MLP-only comparator from v2 Table 5 disappears. The original nine classification HNNs and four hyperlink-prediction HNNs remain; the EDGNN figure label becomes ED-HNN.

E3.justification: v4 adds controlled experiments replacing only the message-passing module with SGC or SIGN while keeping other components fixed. Its new Trivago evaluation reports 64-layer Deep-HGNN for classification and two layers for hyperlink prediction. Existing splits, accuracy/AUC metrics and the 5:1 negative-to-positive ratio remain unchanged; appendix settings are disclosures rather than established revisions.

E4.justification: The new module-replacement study tests the proposed propagation against training-free graph alternatives across four datasets. Conversely, v2's MLP-only ablation testing the benefit of structural propagation is removed. The depth/alpha sensitivity analysis and weighted-versus-unweighted comparison remain, although v4 reverses the latter's row labels.

E5.justification: v4 newly specifies five runs for hyperlink prediction and reports numerical uncertainty for absolute training times in Tables 4–5, 10 and 12. Ten classification runs and existing score uncertainty are retained. The five-run statement is new disclosure, not evidence of increased repetitions; neither PDF clearly defines the meaning of all ± values.

E6.justification: The original six-dataset classification scores are identical, but v4 adds substantial results for new benchmarks and comparators. Trivago classification reports 94.03% for TF-HNN versus 84.06% for Deep-HGNN, with training times of 38.09 versus 3352.35 seconds. Appendix J adds hyperlink results, including ED-HNN outperforming TF-HNN on Senate. MLP-only and CE-homophily entries disappear. Table 7 assigns retained ablation scores to opposite weighted/unweighted labels, contradicting its discussion.

T1.justification: Relative to v2's available statements and proof sketches, v4 supplies extensive formal material in Appendices B–H and M: mechanism-specific derivations, propagation-support proofs, explicit weighting assumptions, entropy arguments and the limiting optimisation derivation. Most main mathematical results are retained or reformulated; Proposition 3.3 adds an explicit i != j restriction. This establishes expanded documented support, not that every argument was newly developed.

C1.justification: The central efficiency, information-utilisation and oversmoothing claims remain. v4 additionally presents the unified aggregation framework as a distinct contribution, explicitly claims the first decoupling of structural processing from model learning, and replaces the Cora-CA headline example with a large-scale Trivago claim.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations attributing performance to fewer trainable parameters and reduced overfitting, and attributes SIGN's disadvantage to its classifier's feature-merging burden. It adds explicit hyperedge-node importance learning as future work. Existing oversmoothing and heterophily interpretations, and the lack of hypergraph-level evaluation, remain.

D1.justification: Appendices I, K and L supply dataset descriptions, negative-sampling construction and per-dataset model depths, widths, learning rates, alpha and regularisation settings missing from the supplied v2. The text changes promised code release to claimed code/data availability at the TF-HNN address. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementation; settings for Trivago and several added comparisons remain incomplete.

R1.justification: v4 expands positioning through a four-mechanism HNN taxonomy, graph-filter applicability restrictions and optimisation connections, adding references such as Kim et al. (2024), Ortega et al. (2018) and Yang et al. (2021). It strengthens the first-decoupling novelty claim and develops comparisons with training-free graph methods. The earlier SIGN/SGC inspiration and distinction from inference-focused hypergraph methods remain.

P1.justification: The title changes from Simplifying Hypergraph Neural Networks to Training-Free Message Passing for Learning on Hypergraphs. Abstract, introduction and methodological framing are extensively rewritten around MP-Modules and TF-HNN. A method overview is added, discussions are reorganised, and named appendix sections replace unsupported generic appendix references.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws Figure 1, merges method formulas and complexity comparisons into Table 1, and transposes the dataset table while dropping homophily/task fields. It adds experimental and hyperparameter tables and restructures the component ablations. Figures 2–4 largely retain their plotted content with revised sizing and labels.

improvement.justification: The direct SGC/SIGN comparisons and large-scale Trivago experiments address important gaps in evidence for the method's distinctiveness and efficiency. Supplied proofs and reproduction settings substantially improve inspectability over the available v2. These gains outweigh the removed MLP control, incomplete settings for new experiments and Table 7's reversed labels, although those defects weaken reproducibility and the component analysis.
